citation: Jaciw, A. P., Hegseth, W. M., Lin, L., Toby, M., Newman, D., Ma, B., & Zacamy, J. (2016). Assessing impacts of Math in Focus, a 'Singapore Math' program. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 9(4), 473-502. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2016.1164777. Underlying RCT report: Jaciw, A. P., Hegseth, W., Ma, B., & Lai, G. (2012, November). Assessing Impacts of Math in Focus, a 'Singapore Math' Program for American Schools: Findings from an RCT (Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_MIF121130-FR1-Y1-O.1). Palo Alto, CA: Empirical Education Inc.
report_number: Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_MIF121130-FR1-Y1-O.1; published as JREE 9(4):473-502, DOI 10.1080/19345747.2016.1164777; sponsor Houghton Mifflin Harcourt (HMH)
design: Cluster (grade-level-team / Teacher-Class level) randomized controlled trial in Clark County School District, Nevada (a large, predominantly low-income/Title-I district), conducted in school year 2011-12. 12 elementary schools recruited; within each school, grade-level teams (typically a combined grade 4+5 team and a grade 3 team) were randomized within-school (matched-pair blocks) to Math in Focus (MIF) vs business-as-usual control. Altogether 22 grade-level teams were randomized (12 MIF, 10 control). Intervention = Math in Focus (HMH's 'Singapore Math' grades 3-5 elementary mathematics CORE CURRICULUM) plus the accompanying HMH-provided teacher training/professional development (5 sessions across the year delivered by external HMH 'Math in Focus National Specialists' / account & product managers: Aug introduction 1.5-3 h, day-long Sept & Nov grade-level sessions, modeling/debrief Jan, day-long Mar) = 'TPD for curricula', Short duration, External trainer, Zero of the four TPD principles (no coaching cycle / performance standards / self-regulation / cooperation framework). Comparison = business-as-usual (district's existing variety of math methods). Outcome subject = mathematics (STEM); grades 3-5 (registry band 3-6). Three math achievement outcomes: SAT 10 Problem Solving, SAT 10 Procedures (the two SAT-10 Mathematics sections, vertically scaled), and Nevada's Criterion Referenced Test (CRT). Impacts estimated via covariate-adjusted multilevel models (ANCOVA / HLM with random grade-level-team effects and separate school effects, pretest + covariates), which account for the cluster-randomized design. Adjusted (benchmark) effect size = regression-adjusted MIF-minus-control mean difference divided by the control-group posttest SD.
problems: IDENTIFICATION NUANCE (author-string mismatch resolved by attribute matching): The meta-analysis label for registry row 51 is 'Jaciw, Schellinger et al. 2016', but BOTH the published JREE 2016 article and the underlying Empirical Education report front-list Andrew Jaciw and Whitney Hegseth (full JREE author list: Jaciw, Hegseth, Lin, Toby, Newman, Ma, Zacamy; report cover: Jaciw, Hegseth, Ma, Lai). Adam Schellinger is NOT a listed author of the Math in Focus study; Schellinger is instead a co-author of the sibling Empirical Education studies iRAISE (Jaciw, Schellinger, Lin, Zacamy, Toby, 2016 -- registry row 50) and RAISE (Fancsali et al. 2015 -- registry row 29). The two Jaciw-2016 rows in this meta-analysis appear to have had their second-author surnames TRANSPOSED relative to the actual reports: row 50 is labelled 'Jaciw, Hegseth' but its registry attributes (Unpublished; grades 7-12; Average/High SES; Comprehensive approaches; Res/Dev test; Three principles; reading) match iRAISE, whose real second author is Schellinger; row 51 is labelled 'Jaciw, Schellinger' but its registry attributes (Published; grades 3-6; Low SES; TPD for curricula; External trainer; Zero principles; math/STEM) match Math in Focus, whose real second author is Hegseth. I resolved row 51 to Math in Focus on ATTRIBUTES (the meta-analysis's own S3.1/S3.2 coding), which uniquely identify it: only MIF is a PUBLISHED (JREE 2016), grades-3-5, Low-SES (Clark County Title-I), math CORE-CURRICULUM-implementation RCT with external (HMH) trainers and none of the four TPD principles. This is the same attribute-matching logic the iRAISE/row-50 extraction used (it noted iRAISE's real second author is Schellinger, not Hegseth, yet assigned iRAISE to the 'Jaciw, Hegseth' row 50 because attributes matched). MIF and iRAISE are genuinely distinct studies (different subjects, grades, SES, designs), so rows 50 and 51 are not duplicates. NOTE the project's own synthetic FIXTURE row for row 51 is coded outcome_subject=STEM, grade_band=3-6 -- consistent with Math in Focus, not with the reading study iRAISE. YEAR/SOURCE NUANCE: the underlying RCT report is dated November 2012; the meta-analysis cites it as 2016, matching the peer-reviewed JREE publication year. The downloaded PDF is the full Empirical Education report (101 pp) that the JREE article reports; the impact effect sizes (Tables 16-18) are identical to those discussed in the literature for this study. VARIANCE NUANCE: the report gives adjusted effect sizes (the regression-adjusted, cluster-modeled standardized impact) and p-values, but does NOT report a clean SE on the same standardized ES metric (the Table 19 model coefficients, e.g. MIF effect 29.31 SE 0.96, are in raw SAT-10 scale-score units, a different scale than the 0.12 ES). I therefore derived g_se / g_var from the report's stated ACHIEVED (sample-based, model-based) minimum detectable effect sizes, which are on the same standardized metric and already reflect the cluster design + covariate adjustment: MDES = .11 (SAT 10 Problem Solving), .18 (SAT 10 Procedures), .21 (CRT) at alpha=.05, 80% power (footnote 1, p.5). SE = MDES / (z_.975 + z_.80) = MDES / 2.8016. These design-based SEs make cluster_adjusted=true appropriate. NO empirical design-effect ICC is reported: the .15 ICC (p.6) is an a-priori power-analysis assumption (per spec, NOT an observed design-effect ICC), and Table 19's residual team variance (9.23 / (9.23+570.99) = 0.016) is a covariate-conditional within-grade-z residual ICC, not the unconditional design-effect ICC -- so icc is left null per spec. CLUSTER COUNTS: n_clusters = number of grade-level teams contributing to each analytic sample (from Tables 16-18): 18 teams (9 MIF + 9 control) for both SAT-10 outcomes, 20 teams (11 MIF + 9 control) for the CRT. ATTRITION: 18.18% overall team-level attrition (3/12 MIF, 1/10 control teams lost) and ~26.6% student-level attrition; the report's own sensitivity analyses found the Problem Solving result NOT robust to all model specifications (p ranged .05-.26), so confidence in the precise magnitude of the headline ES is moderate even though identification is high.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Math in Focus (Singapore Math) curriculum + HMH teacher training vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Stanford Achievement Test, 10th ed. (SAT 10) - Mathematics Problem Solving section
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2012 (end of one-year implementation, immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's headline pretest-/covariate-adjusted effect size = 0.12 (Table 16, p.54): regression-adjusted (ANCOVA/HLM benchmark) MIF-minus-control mean difference on the SAT 10 Problem Solving scale, standardized by the control-group posttest SD; model includes random grade-level-team effects (cluster-randomized design) + pretest + covariates. Hedges' g = J*d, J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1639, J = 0.99954, so g = 0.99954*0.12 = 0.1199 ~ 0.12 (small-sample correction negligible). g_se/g_var derived from the report's ACHIEVED sample-based MDES = 0.11 SD for this outcome (footnote 1, p.5; alpha=.05, 80% power): SE = 0.11/2.8016 = 0.0393, g_var = SE^2 = 0.00154; this design-based SE is on the same standardized metric as the ES and reflects the teacher/team-level clustering. impact_estimate holds the adjusted ES (0.12) and impact_se the same design-based SE. mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c are the UNADJUSTED descriptive posttest scale-score means/SDs from Table 16 (Control 639.96/43.05; MIF 634.23/40.62) -- note the unadjusted ES is -0.14 (favoring control) before pretest adjustment; the report's own cluster-corrected unadjusted Hedges' g (Hedges 2007) is -0.14.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 16 (p.54): adjusted ES = 0.12, p=.05; unadjusted means/SDs/Ns/teams/schools; MDES footnote 1 (p.5).
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY full-sample confirmatory TPD-for-curricula vs business-as-usual student math contrast (the report's pre-registered headline expectation: a positive impact on SAT 10 Problem Solving, the depth/problem-solving-oriented outcome best aligned with the MIF/Singapore-Math/CCSS approach). Adjusted ES = +0.12 (p=.05); unadjusted (cluster-corrected) ES = -0.14 (p=.55) -- the sign flips after pretest adjustment because MIF teams happened to have lower-achieving students at baseline. Per-outcome analytic sample: 1641 students (857 MIF / 784 control) in 18 grade-level teams (9/9) across 18 school-entries (9/9). The report's sensitivity analyses found the Problem Solving impact NOT robust to all model specifications (p ranged .05-.26, Appendix C). The MIF effect did NOT vary by pretest level (Table 19 interaction coef 0.04, p=.97) or by minority status. TEACHER/IMPLEMENTATION outcomes (NOT student achievement, excluded per spec) and moderation analyses are reported separately.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Math in Focus (Singapore Math) curriculum + HMH teacher training vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Stanford Achievement Test, 10th ed. (SAT 10) - Mathematics Procedures section
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2012 (end of one-year implementation, immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's pretest-/covariate-adjusted effect size = 0.14 (Table 17, p.55): regression-adjusted (ANCOVA/HLM benchmark) MIF-minus-control mean difference on the SAT 10 Procedures scale, standardized by the control-group posttest SD; random grade-level-team effects + pretest + covariates. Hedges' g = J*d, df = 1625, J = 0.99954, g = 0.99954*0.14 = 0.1399 ~ 0.14. g_se/g_var from the achieved sample-based MDES = 0.18 SD for this outcome (footnote 1, p.5): SE = 0.18/2.8016 = 0.0642, g_var = 0.00413. mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c are the unadjusted descriptive posttest scale-score means/SDs from Table 17 (Control 634.28/47.33; MIF 630.59/45.05); unadjusted cluster-corrected ES = -0.08.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 17 (p.55): adjusted ES = 0.14, p=.10; unadjusted means/SDs/Ns; MDES footnote 1 (p.5).
effect_sizes.notes: SECONDARY full-sample TPD-for-curricula vs business-as-usual student math contrast on the SAT 10 Procedures (computation) section. The report a priori EXPECTED a smaller or no impact here (procedures/breadth, less aligned with MIF's depth focus), but observed adjusted ES = +0.14 (p=.10); unadjusted (cluster-corrected) ES = -0.08 (p=.69). Analytic sample 1627 students (835 MIF / 792 control), 18 grade-level teams (9/9). Sensitivity p ranged .09-.68 (not robust to all specifications). SAT 10 Problem Solving and SAT 10 Procedures are the two sections of the SAT 10 Mathematics test but are analyzed as separate outcomes; the report does not report a SAT 10 Mathematics total/composite, so this is recorded as a distinct outcome rather than a subscale of an extracted composite.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Math in Focus (Singapore Math) curriculum + HMH teacher training vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Nevada Criterion Referenced Test (CRT) - Mathematics (state criterion-referenced test; z-transformed within grade for analysis)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2012 (end of one-year implementation, immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's pretest-/covariate-adjusted effect size = 0.05 (Table 18, p.57): regression-adjusted (ANCOVA/HLM benchmark) MIF-minus-control mean difference on the (within-grade z-transformed) Nevada CRT, standardized by the control-group posttest SD; random grade-level-team effects + pretest + covariates. Because the CRT is not vertically scaled, the report z-transformed posttests within grade (control mean 0, SD 1), so the descriptive means/SDs are in z-units. Hedges' g = J*d, df = 2065, J = 0.99964, g = 0.99964*0.05 = 0.0500 ~ 0.05. g_se/g_var from the achieved sample-based MDES = 0.21 SD for this outcome (footnote 1, p.5): SE = 0.21/2.8016 = 0.0750, g_var = 0.00562. mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c are the unadjusted descriptive z-scaled posttest means/SDs from Table 18 (Control 0.00/1.00; MIF -0.02/1.07); unadjusted cluster-corrected ES = -0.02.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 18 (p.57): adjusted ES = 0.05, p=.54; unadjusted z-scaled means/SDs/Ns; MDES footnote 1 (p.5).
effect_sizes.notes: SECONDARY full-sample TPD-for-curricula vs business-as-usual student math contrast on the Nevada state CRT (math). The report a priori expected NO positive impact on the state test (Nevada standards/test not fully shifted to CCSS), and indeed adjusted ES = +0.05 (p=.54, no confidence in a real difference); unadjusted (cluster-corrected) ES = -0.02 (p=.88). Largest analytic sample: 2067 students (1126 MIF / 941 control) in 20 grade-level teams (11 MIF / 9 control), 20 school-entries (11/9). Sensitivity p ranged .28-.91; all consistent with no impact. The CRT is the most-independent of the three measures (an off-the-shelf state criterion-referenced test).
